**Setup.** Place the rectangle with A=(0,0), B=(a,0), C=(a,b), D=(0,b). Any choice of 3 sides from 4 must include one pair of opposite sides. By symmetry, two cases suffice:

- **Type I:** Vertices on the two horizontal sides (y=0, y=b) and one vertical side (x=a).
- **Type II:** Vertices on the two vertical sides (x=0, x=a) and one horizontal side (y=0).

---

**Type I Analysis.** Let P=(p,0) on bottom, Q=(a,q) on right, R=(r,b) on top, forming an equilateral triangle. Using the rotation characterization: Q = P + R_{−60°}(R − P).

Computing: R − P = (r−p, b), and R_{−60°}(r−p, b) = ((r−p)/2 + b√3/2, −(r−p)√3/2 + b/2).

So Q = ((p+r)/2 + b√3/2, (p−r)√3/2 + b/2).

**Constraint from Q on x = a:** (p+r)/2 + b√3/2 = a, giving p + r = 2a − b√3. ...(*)

**Constraint from 0 ≤ q ≤ b:** −b/√3 ≤ r − p ≤ b/√3. ...(**)

Let d = r − p. The side length is s = √(d² + b²), so maximizing s means maximizing |d|.

From (*): p = (2a − b√3 − d)/2, r = (2a − b√3 + d)/2. Requiring 0 ≤ p ≤ a and 0 ≤ r ≤ a yields:
- d ≤ 2a − b√3, d ≥ b√3 − 2a, d ≤ b√3, d ≥ −b√3.

Combined with (**): d ∈ [max(−b/√3, b√3−2a), min(b/√3, 2a−b√3)].

**Subcase A:** a ≥ 2b/√3 (i.e., b ≤ a√3/2). Then 2a−b√3 ≥ b/√3 and b√3−2a ≤ −b/√3, so d ∈ [−b/√3, b/√3]. Max |d| = b/√3, giving s² = 4b²/3 and **Area = b²/√3**.

**Subcase B:** b√3/2 ≤ a < 2b/√3 (i.e., a√3/2 < b ≤ 2a/√3). Then d ∈ [b√3−2a, 2a−b√3]. Max |d| = 2a − b√3, giving s² = (2a−b√3)² + b² = 4(a² − ab√3 + b²) and **Area = √3(a² − ab√3 + b²) = √3a² − 3ab + √3b²**.

**Subcase C:** a < b√3/2 (i.e., b > 2a/√3). The interval is empty — no solution.

(The other rotation direction R₊₆₀° gives p + r = 2a + b√3 > 2a, contradicting p, r ≤ a, so no valid configuration.)

---

**Type II Analysis.** By the symmetry of swapping a ↔ b (rotating the rectangle 90°), Type II with rectangle a×b is identical to Type I with rectangle b×a. Therefore:

- b ≥ 2a/√3: **Area = a²/√3**
- a√3/2 ≤ b < 2a/√3: **Area = √3a² − 3ab + √3b²**
- b < a√3/2: no solution

---

**Combining both types.** Taking the maximum over all valid configurations:

$$S_{\max} = \begin{cases} \dfrac{b^2}{\sqrt{3}} & \text{if } b \leq \dfrac{a\sqrt{3}}{2} \\[8pt] \sqrt{3}\,a^2 - 3ab + \sqrt{3}\,b^2 & \text{if } \dfrac{a\sqrt{3}}{2} \leq b \leq \dfrac{2a}{\sqrt{3}} \\[8pt] \dfrac{a^2}{\sqrt{3}} & \text{if } b \geq \dfrac{2a}{\sqrt{3}} \end{cases}$$

**Continuity verification.** At b = a√3/2: b²/√3 = 3a²/(4√3) = a²√3/4, and √3a² − 3a(a√3/2) + √3(3a²/4) = √3a²(1 − 3/2 + 3/4) = a²√3/4. ✓ At b = 2a/√3: √3a² − 3a(2a/√3) + √3(4a²/3) = √3a²(1 − 2 + 4/3) = a²√3/3 = a²/√3. ✓

**Geometric interpretation.** In the first regime (b ≤ a√3/2), the maximum is achieved by placing one side of the equilateral triangle along the bottom (or top) of the rectangle with length s = 2b/√3 (so the triangle height equals b), with one base vertex at a corner. The condition a ≥ 2b/√3 ensures this base fits within the width. The third regime is the analogous configuration rotated 90°. The middle regime requires a tilted equilateral triangle.

**Role of the constraint a > 2/√3.** Under the natural interpretation that the condition is a > 2b/√3 (i.e., the rectangle is wide enough relative to its height), we are in the first regime, and the maximum area is:

$$\boxed{\dfrac{b^2}{\sqrt{3}}}$$

This is achieved by the equilateral triangle with side length s = 2b/√3, whose height s√3/2 = b exactly spans the rectangle's height, with one side resting on a horizontal side of the rectangle and one vertex at a corner.
